numberItems.stem: Where are the federal Hazardous Materials Regulations (HMR) found?
numberItems.explanation: The HMR are in CFR, Title 49, Parts 171–180. §172.101 is only the Hazardous Materials Table, and §383.5 defines HazMat for the "H" endorsement (p. 9-1).

numberItems.stem: [CA] Under CVC §27903, what will DMV examiners NOT do?
options: Give a CDL skills test in a vehicle showing placards
Give a CDL skills test in a vehicle with air brakes
Give a CDL skills test in a school bus
numberItems.explanation: [CA] DMV examiners will not give CDL skills tests in a placarded vehicle, including one not yet purged of hazardous cargo (CVC §27903) (p. 9-1).

numberItems.stem: How long must your employer keep your HazMat training record?
options: While you work with HazMat, plus 1 year
While you work with HazMat, plus 90 days
numberItems.explanation: The employer keeps the training record for as long as the employee works with HazMat, plus 90 days (p. 9-2).

numberItems.stem: When must you pass a TSA security threat assessment (background records check)?
options: Only the first time you get the "H" endorsement
When you apply for a new or renewed "H" endorsement
numberItems.explanation: A TSA background records check is required when you apply for a new "H" endorsement or renew one. You give fingerprints, a fee and 1 ID document (p. 9-2).

numberItems.stem: [CA] Besides loads that must show placards, which HazMat loads need a CHP HazMat transportation license?
options: Loads over 500 lb hauled for a fee that would need placards in larger amounts
Loads over 1,001 lb, whether or not hauled for a fee
Any HazMat load of any size, even hauled free
numberItems.explanation: [CA] The CHP license covers placarded loads and loads over 500 lb hauled for a fee that would need placards if shipped in larger amounts (CVC §32000.5) (p. 9-2).

numberItems.stem: At least how many identical placards must a placarded vehicle show?
options: 4, on the front, rear and both sides
numberItems.explanation: A placarded vehicle needs at least 4 identical placards, front, rear and both sides, readable from all 4 directions (p. 9-5).

numberItems.stem: What is the minimum size of a placard?
options: Any size, as long as it can be read from 4 directions
The same size as the package label
At least 9.84 in (250 mm) square, turned on point
numberItems.explanation: Placards must be at least 9.84 inches (250 mm) square, turned square-on-point like a diamond (p. 9-5).

numberItems.stem: How many digits does a HazMat ID number have?
numberItems.explanation: An ID number is a 4-digit code that follows "UN", "NA" or "ID" (p. 9-5).

numberItems.stem: Before you haul a material, how many lists should you check to see if it is regulated?
options: 3: the HazMat Table, Appendix A and Appendix B
numberItems.explanation: Check 3 lists: the Hazardous Materials Table, Appendix A (hazardous substances and RQs) and Appendix B (marine pollutants). Some materials are on all 3, some on only one (p. 9-5).

numberItems.stem: How many different symbols may appear in Column 1 of the Hazardous Materials Table?
numberItems.explanation: Column 1 may show 6 symbols: +, A, W, D, I and G (p. 9-5).

numberItems.stem: What does Column 8 of the Hazardous Materials Table give?
options: The packing group, in Roman numerals
The section numbers for packaging rules, in 3 parts
numberItems.explanation: Column 8 is a 3-part column giving the section numbers for packaging rules. Packing groups are Column 5; codes 1–6 are in Column 7 (p. 9-6).

numberItems.stem: When must the shipper show "RQ" on the shipping paper and package?
options: When 1 package holds the reportable quantity or more
When the whole load together reaches the reportable quantity
numberItems.explanation: "RQ" is shown when 1 package holds the reportable quantity of an Appendix A hazardous substance or more (p. 9-6).

numberItems.stem: In the handbook's Appendix A example, what is the reportable quantity (RQ) of phosgene?
numberItems.explanation: Figure 9.5 lists phosgene at 10 lb; 100 lb is phosphine and 5,000 lb is phosphoric acid (p. 9-6).

numberItems.stem: For highway shipping, the marine pollutant list is used only for containers of what size (without HMR placards or labels)?
numberItems.explanation: For highway shipping, Appendix B is used only for chemicals in a container of 119 gallons or more without a placard or label as the HMR specify (p. 9-7).

numberItems.stem: At minimum, how many kinds of facts must emergency response information cover?
numberItems.explanation: ERI covers at least 7 kinds of facts, from the basic description to basic first aid, and must be usable away from the vehicle (p. 9-8).

numberItems.stem: How long must a shipper keep a copy of the shipping paper for HazMat that is NOT hazardous waste?
numberItems.explanation: Shippers keep a copy for 2 years after the first carrier accepts the material, or 3 years for hazardous waste (p. 9-8).

numberItems.stem: A carrier is only providing carrier service and did not start the shipment. How long does the carrier keep a copy of the shipping paper?
numberItems.explanation: In the carrier-service-only case, the carrier keeps a copy for 1 year (p. 9-8).

numberItems.stem: In the description "10 ctns., UN1263, Paint, 3, PG II, 500 pounds", what does the "3" stand for?
numberItems.explanation: The basic description is ID number (UN1263), proper shipping name (Paint), hazard class (3), packing group (PG II); "10 ctns." is the package count (p. 9-8).

numberItems.stem: How should hazardous waste acetone be described on the shipping paper?
numberItems.explanation: For hazardous waste, the word WASTE goes before the proper shipping name: UN1090, Waste Acetone, 3, PG II (p. 9-8).
